cues.zh: 大家好……
cues.en: Hey, guys...

cues.zh: 所以我决定做一个视频系列，专门讲动画的12条原则，
cues.en: So, I decided to make a video series dedicated to the 12 principles of animation,

cues.zh: 由传奇动画师Frank Thomas和Ollie Johnston提出。
cues.en: as described by the legendary animators Frank Thomas and Ollie Johnston.

cues.zh: 第一条原则是“挤压与拉伸”。
cues.en: So the first principle is "squash and stretch".

cues.zh: 这条原则是说，动画对象会被拉长
cues.en: This is the principle that animated objects will get longer

cues.zh: 或压扁，以强调它们的速度、动量、重量和质量。
cues.en: or flatter to emphasize their speed, momentum, weight, and mass.

cues.zh: 这是一个有挤压与拉伸的弹跳球。
cues.en: Here's a bouncing ball that has squash and stretch.

cues.zh: 而这个是没有挤压与拉伸的。
cues.en: And here is one without squash and stretch.

cues.zh: 看出区别了吗？
cues.en: See the difference?

cues.zh: 一个物体挤压与拉伸的程度，能说明它的质量。
cues.en: The amount that an object squashes and stretches says something about its mass.

cues.zh: 挤压与拉伸越多，物体越柔软。
cues.en: The more squash and stretch, the softer the object.

cues.zh: 挤压与拉伸越少，物体越僵硬。
cues.en: The less squash and stretch, the stiffer the object.

cues.zh: 第一个看起来像水气球，第二个大概就是保龄球了。
cues.en: This first one looks like a water balloon and the second one probably would be a bowling ball.

cues.zh: 挤压与拉伸也适用于角色。
cues.en: Squash and stretch applies to characters, too.

cues.zh: 看这个人物下落时因速度而拉伸，
cues.en: Look at how this figure is stretching from the speed that he's coming down with,

cues.zh: 落地后挤压，再稳定到姿势。
cues.en: and then he squashes after he lands before settling in his pose.

cues.zh: 你也可以用挤压与拉伸来夸张面部表情。
cues.en: You can also use squash and stretch to exaggerate facial expressions.

cues.zh: 让我们给这张脸加一些挤压与拉伸：
cues.en: Let's add some squash and stretch to this face:

cues.zh: 当他闭眼时，脸是挤压的，
cues.en: when his eyes are closed, his face is squashed,

cues.zh: 而当他难以置信地睁眼时，
cues.en: and when he opens his eyes in disbelief,

cues.zh: 脸向上拉伸，再恢复常态。
cues.en: his face stretches up and settles back to normal.

cues.zh: 保持物体体积一致非常重要。
cues.en: It's very important to keep the volume of the object consistent.

cues.zh: 很多人刚开始尝试“挤压与拉伸”时都会搞错这一点。
cues.en: This is what a lot of people mess up with when they're first trying to do "squash and stretch".

cues.zh: 他们会像这样把球拉长，像这样压扁。
cues.en: They'll elongate the ball like this, and flatten it like this.

cues.zh: 这是你不应该做的。
cues.en: This is what you should NOT do.

cues.zh: 球的总体积必须保持不变：
cues.en: The overall volume of the ball must be the same:

cues.zh: 所以球变长时，也会变窄；
cues.en: so as the ball gets longer, it also gets narrower;

cues.zh: 变扁时，也会变宽。
cues.en: when it gets flatter, it also gets wider.

cues.zh: 立方体也是一样。
cues.en: The same goes with cubes.

cues.zh: 如果一条线向内收，其他线就必须朝相反方向走。
cues.en: If you're going in with one line, the other lines must go in the opposite direction.

cues.zh: 立方体应该从窄开始，变扁，再变窄，然后停住。
cues.en: The cube should start out narrow, get flat, get narrow again, and then rest.

cues.zh: 用立方体做中间帧很容易，因为你可以测量两条线之间的那条线
cues.en: In -betweening with cubes is easy because you can measure the line in between the two lines

cues.zh: 然后把它们连起来，做出立方体。
cues.en: and then connect them to make the cube.

cues.zh: 如果你掌握了立方体的“挤压与拉伸”，下一步就是尝试在3D中做。
cues.en: If you master "squash and stretch" with cubes, the next step is to try to do it in 3D.

cues.zh: 另一个重要提示是，球不必在整个下落过程中都保持拉伸。
cues.en: Another important note is that the ball does not have to be stretching the entire time that it's falling.

cues.zh: 刚开始下落时，它大部分时间应该保持正常形状，
cues.en: When it's just starting to fall, it should have its normal shape for the most part,

cues.zh: 然后当它即将触底时，
cues.en: and then when it's just about to hit the bottom,

cues.zh: 那才是拉伸最大的时候。
cues.en: that's when it has the most stretch.

cues.zh: 所以，从这个意义上说，不要过度使用“挤压与拉伸”。
cues.en: So, do not overdo "squash and stretch" in this sense.

cues.zh: 好！动画的第二个原则叫做预备动作。
cues.en: Alright! The second principle of animation is called Anticipation.

cues.zh: 就是角色在做动作前先做准备，给观众一个线索
cues.en: This is when a character prepares for an action to give the audience a clue

cues.zh: 提示接下来要发生什么
cues.en: as to what is happening next

cues.zh: 同时也让动作看起来更真实。
cues.en: As well as to make the action appear more realistic.

cues.zh: 举个例子，角色准备起跳时。
cues.en: One example is when a character is about to jump.

cues.zh: 在跃向空中之前，他必须先做准备动作
cues.en: Before leaping into the air, he has to prepare for the action

cues.zh: 蹲下来蓄力。
cues.en: by crouching down to build energy.

cues.zh: 就像弹簧先压缩再释放。
cues.en: It's like a spring that coils up before releasing.

cues.zh: 看这个角色起跳时完全没有预备动作。
cues.en: Look at this character jumping without any anticipation.

cues.zh: 看起来很不真实，因为起跳的力量凭空而来。
cues.en: It looks very unrealistic because the energy to jump comes out of nowhere.

cues.zh: 再看一个例子：出拳。
cues.en: Here's another example: a punch.

cues.zh: 为了增加出拳的力量，并告诉观众他要出拳了。
cues.en: To add power to the punch and communicate to the viewers that he is about to punch.

cues.zh: 他先把手臂收回，然后再出拳。
cues.en: He reaches his arm back and then punches.

cues.zh: 相比之下，没有预备动作，出拳就会显得非常无力。
cues.en: By contrast having no anticipation results in a very weak punch.

cues.zh: 你会在很多动画里看到这一点：角色起跑前会先蓄力，然后才冲出去。
cues.en: You'll see this in a lot of cartoons before running a character will wind up, before taking off.

cues.zh: 之前讲挤压与拉伸的那期视频里，这张脸其实也用到了预备动作。
cues.en: In the previous video about squash and stretch this face actually uses anticipation as well.

cues.zh: 它不是立刻向上拉伸，而是先挤压一下，为拉伸做预备，
cues.en: Instead of immediately stretching up, the face squashes first to anticipate the stretch

cues.zh: 从而让它更有力量。
cues.en: and give it more power.

cues.zh: 预备动作能帮助把动作传达给观众，让他们为下一个动作做好准备。
cues.en: Anticipation helps communicate actions to the audience by preparing them for the next action.

cues.zh: 这可以通过很多方式实现
cues.en: This can happen in many ways

cues.zh: 如果一个角色要从口袋里掏东西，
cues.en: If a character is about to take something out of their pocket.

cues.zh: 他们会先把手举到空中、让手非常显眼，然后再伸进口袋。
cues.en: They make their hand very visible and up in the air before going into the pocket.

cues.zh: 否则观众可能会错过这个动作，还会纳闷那东西到底是怎么来的。
cues.en: Otherwise the audience might miss it and wonder how they got that object in the first place.

cues.zh: 最重要的是让观众注意到手和口袋
cues.en: The most important thing is that the viewer notices the hand and the pocket

cues.zh: 所以角色不能同时做其他动作。
cues.en: so the character cannot be performing any competing actions.

cues.zh: 假设右边即将发生某件事。
cues.en: Let's say that something is about to happen on the right.

cues.zh: 角色可能会通过眼睛和头部朝向那个方向来为那个动作做准备
cues.en: A character may prepare for that action by pointing their eyes and head to look in that direction

cues.zh: 引导观众也看向那里
cues.en: leading the viewers to also look there

cues.zh: 重要的是尽可能让观众轻松理解正在发生什么
cues.en: It's important to make it as easy as possible for the audience to understand what's going on

cues.zh: 而不必看两遍。
cues.en: without having to watch it twice.

cues.zh: 但这也可以用来欺骗观众。
cues.en: But this can also be used to trick the audience too.

cues.zh: 如果你把他们的视线引向一个方向
cues.en: If you lead their eyes in One direction

cues.zh: 然后让屏幕另一侧发生某事来给他们惊喜。
cues.en: and then surprise them by having something happen on the other side of the screen.

cues.zh: 把预期推进一步
cues.en: Taking anticipation of step further

cues.zh: 你实际上可以设置多个层次的预期
cues.en: you can actually have multiple levels of anticipation

cues.zh: 让我们回到出拳动画，角色在出拳前会蓄力。
cues.en: Let's go back to our punch animation where the character winds up before punching.

cues.zh: 这个动画只有一层预备动作
cues.en: This animation has one level of anticipation

cues.zh: 现在看这个。
cues.en: Now look at this one.

cues.zh: 这个角色其实是在为他的蓄力动作做反向蓄势
cues.en: The character is actually winding out for his wind-up

cues.zh: 先向前，再蓄力，然后在出拳之前
cues.en: by going forward then winding up and then before punching

cues.zh: 他把另一只手臂向后甩，进一步为这一拳做预备。
cues.en: he throws his other arm back to further anticipate the punch.

cues.zh: 这一拳非常复杂。
cues.en: This punch is very complex.

cues.zh: 它其实类似于棒球投手准备投球时的动作。
cues.en: It's actually similar to what a baseball pitcher does when he's getting ready to throw the ball.

cues.zh: 所以动画的第三条原则叫做布局。
cues.en: So the third principle of animation is called staging.

cues.zh: 布局是把任何想法呈现出来，使其完全且明确无误地清晰。
cues.en: Staging is the presentation of any idea so that it is completely and unmistakably clear.

cues.zh: 这是一条非常宽泛的原则，因为它涵盖了动画的许多方面。
cues.en: This is a very broad principle because it covers so many areas of animation.

cues.zh: 它可以应用于表演、时间节奏、镜头角度和位置以及场景布置。
cues.en: It can apply to acting, timing, camera Angle and position and setting.

cues.zh: 所以做动画时，你要完全掌控观众的视线落在哪里。
cues.en: So when you're animating you want to be in full control of where the audience is looking.

cues.zh: 你本质上是在说，看这个，
cues.en: You're essentially saying look at this,

cues.zh: 现在看这个
cues.en: now look at this

cues.zh: 现在再看这个。
cues.en: and now look at this.

cues.zh: 这种控制是通过场面调度实现的。
cues.en: This control is achieved through staging.

cues.zh: 场景中的所有元素共同作用，引导观众的视线在屏幕上移动。
cues.en: All of the elements of the scene work together to move the viewers eyes around the screen.

cues.zh: 这是一个糟糕调度的例子。
cues.en: Here's an example of bad staging.

cues.zh: 角色们都在争夺画面存在感，观众不知道该看哪一个。
cues.en: The characters are competing for stage presence, so the viewer doesn't know which one to look at.

cues.zh: 镜头对此有很大影响。
cues.en: The camera has a lot to do with this.

cues.zh: 重要的是要知道什么时候该用近景，什么时候该用远景。
cues.en: It's important to know when to be closed up and went to be far away.

cues.zh: 远景适合大动作，而近景适合表情。
cues.en: Far away is good for big actions while close-up is good for expressions.

cues.zh: 不要让主要动作偏在画面一侧。
cues.en: Don't have the main action be off to the side.

cues.zh: 它应该要么在屏幕中央，要么在屏幕的三分之一线上。
cues.en: It should be either in the center of the screen or in one of the thirds of the screen.

cues.zh: 如果他们面朝侧面
cues.en: If they're facing to the side

cues.zh: 那么他们面朝的方向应该留出更多空白
cues.en: there should be more empty space in the direction that they're facing

cues.zh: 除非有人从背后悄悄靠近
cues.en: Unless someone's sneaking it behind them

cues.zh: 那样的话，他们就不再是这个镜头的主角了。
cues.en: in which case they would no longer be the main character of the shot.

cues.zh: 场景的主要动作应该非常清晰简单。
cues.en: The main action of the scene should be very clear and simple.

cues.zh: 不能被其他正在发生的事情抢了风头。
cues.en: It can't be upstaged by other things that are going on.

cues.zh: 这会分散对主要内容的注意力。
cues.en: This takes attention away from the main point.

cues.zh: 还要有恰当的时机。
cues.en: It should also have proper timing.

cues.zh: 让一个动作完成之后，另一个人再开始自己的动作，而不是让它们重叠。
cues.en: Let one action finish before the other person starts their action instead of overlapping them

cues.zh: 有时你需要插入停顿，如果屏幕上有什么东西
cues.en: Sometimes you need to insert pauses if there's something on the screen

cues.zh: 需要观众先消化再继续。
cues.en: that needs to be processed by the viewer before moving on.

cues.zh: 有时如果屏幕上有任何文字。
cues.en: Sometimes if there's any text on the screen.

cues.zh: 你应该让它在屏幕上停留足够长的时间，以便大声读三遍。
cues.en: You should keep it on screen for as long as it takes to read it out loud three times.

cues.zh: 但这不仅仅是控制观众的视线。
cues.en: But it's not just about controlling the viewers eyes.

cues.zh: 还关乎传达想法。
cues.en: It's also about conveying ideas.

cues.zh: 比如如果一个角色很悲伤。
cues.en: If a character is sad for example.

cues.zh: 你要确保观众知道这一点并感受到它。
cues.en: You want to make sure that the viewer knows that and feels that.

cues.zh: 如果设定某人的房子非常破旧简陋。
cues.en: If someone's house is supposed to be very poor and decrepit.

cues.zh: 就要做到极致，确保观众能看出来，
cues.en: Go over the top to make sure that they get it

cues.zh: 不能有任何削弱这一目的的物品。
cues.en: and don't have any objects that detract from that purpose.

cues.zh: 让我们拿这个场景来做舞台化处理。
cues.en: Let's take this scene and give it the staging treatment.

cues.zh: 这个胖子在吃披萨，我们想传达的是
cues.en: This fat guy is eating pizza the idea that we want to convey

cues.zh: 他是个严重的暴食者。
cues.en: is that he is a severe over eater.

cues.zh: 那我们再把场景布置得更充分些。
cues.en: So let's set the stage more.

cues.zh: 多给他些披萨，在他身后堆满披萨盒，
cues.en: Let's give them more pizza and put piles of pizza boxes behind him

cues.zh: 衬衫上还有污渍。
cues.en: and stains on his shirt.

cues.zh: 把摄像机移到他下方，让他显得更大。
cues.en: Let's move the camera down below him to make him look bigger.

cues.zh: 再改改他的表演，让他的体重真正妨碍他吃东西。
cues.en: And let's change his acting so that his weight actually gets in the way of his eating.

cues.zh: 他连伸手拿汽水都会摔倒。
cues.en: So he can't even reach for the soda without falling over.

cues.zh: 现在要确保时间点卡准。
cues.en: Now let's make sure to time it right.

cues.zh: 他注意到汽水，然后伸手去拿。
cues.en: So he notices the soda and then reaches for it.

cues.zh: 现在思路很清晰了。
cues.en: Now the idea is very clear.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: All right.

cues.zh: 第四个动画原则叫做连续绘制和姿势到姿势。
cues.en: So the fourth animation principle is called straight ahead and pose to pose.

cues.zh: 这个术语描述了两种制作动画画面的方法。
cues.en: This term describes two methods used to animate drawings.

cues.zh: 第一种方法“连续绘制”，就是你先画第一张
cues.en: The first method straight ahead is where you draw the first drawing

cues.zh: 然后画第二张，再画第三张，以此类推。
cues.en: and then you draw the second drawing and then the third drawing and so on.

cues.zh: 基本上就是边画边推进动画。
cues.en: It's basically animating as you go.

cues.zh: 第二种方法“姿势到姿势”，就是你先画出每个主要姿势的起始
cues.en: The second method post a pose is where you draw the beginning

cues.zh: 和结束画面，之后再回头补上中间的画
cues.en: and end of each main pose and go back later to fill in the drawings in between

cues.zh: 所以两种方法各有好处。
cues.en: So there are benefits to both methods.

cues.zh: 姿势到姿势通常更适合大多数动作
cues.en: Pose to pose is generally better for most actions

cues.zh: 因为它能给你最大的控制力。
cues.en: because it gives you the most control.

cues.zh: 在制作早期你就能清楚知道动作会是什么样子。
cues.en: You have a good idea of what the action is going to look like very early in the process.

cues.zh: 这样就不用担心角色最后会不会落在正确的位置。
cues.en: So instead of worrying if the character is going to end up in the right place.

cues.zh: 一开始就决定它们的落点，再倒推着做。
cues.en: You decide where they end up from the beginning and work backwards.

cues.zh: 另外
cues.en: Also

cues.zh: 用顺画法动画，角色可能会改变大小
cues.en: Using straight ahead animation can lead to the character changing size

cues.zh: 或者从头到尾处于不同的高度。
cues.en: or being on a different level from beginning to end.

cues.zh: 姿势到姿势能帮你省下大量工作。
cues.en: Pose to pose can save you a lot of work.

cues.zh: 如果你用顺画法把整段序列都画出来
cues.en: If you were to animate a whole sequence straight ahead

cues.zh: 然后发现有一个姿势不对。
cues.en: and then realize that one pose is off.

cues.zh: 你就得改好几张图来修正那一个姿势。
cues.en: You would have to change several drawings to fix that one pose.

cues.zh: 但用姿势到姿势，你先画主要姿势看感觉对不对，
cues.en: But with pose to pose you do the main poses to see if it feels right,

cues.zh: 这样能及早发现问题。
cues.en: and you can catch problems early on.

cues.zh: 另一方面，顺画法适合不可预测的动画。
cues.en: Straight ahead animation on the other hand is good for animation that is unpredictable.

cues.zh: 例子包括火焰、
cues.en: Some examples of this include fire,

cues.zh: 水粒子、尘云、爆炸。
cues.en: water particles, clouds of dust, explosions.

cues.zh: 顺画法之所以好用，是因为物理规律以恒定速率运作。
cues.en: The reason why straight ahead works well is because there are laws of physics that work at a constant rate.

cues.zh: 很难预测姿势到姿势之后会怎样运作。
cues.en: And it's hard to predict how it will work post a pose.

cues.zh: 比如给火焰做动画时。
cues.en: So when animating fire for example.

cues.zh: 你就凭着对火的了解顺其自然地画
cues.en: You just go with the flow based on what you know about fire

cues.zh: 让火焰自己生长出来。
cues.en: and let the fire kind of create itself.

cues.zh: 如果只看开头和结尾，
cues.en: If we were to look at the beginning and end,

cues.zh: 我们根本不知道怎么画出中间过程。
cues.en: we wouldn't even know how to in between it.

cues.zh: 不过，你仍然可以用姿势到姿势法画出大致形状
cues.en: However, you can still use pose to pose to make the general shapes

cues.zh: 再补上中间帧让它更流畅。
cues.en: and fill it in between to make it smoother.

cues.zh: 另一个不可预测动画的例子是重叠动作
cues.en: Another example of unpredictable animation is overlapping action

cues.zh: 下一期视频会深入讲解。
cues.en: which will be covered in depth in the next video.

cues.zh: 假设一个角色有松软的耳朵。
cues.en: Let's say that a character has floppy ears.

cues.zh: 你可以每个姿势都画出带耳朵的角色，再相应画出中间帧。
cues.en: You could draw the figure with his ears for each pose and just draw the in-betweens accordingly.

cues.en: This man is leaning from one shoulder to the other.

cues.zh: 没有中间帧时，看起来像是他的头被
cues.en: With no in-betweens it looks like his head is being hit

cues.zh: 一股巨大的力量击中，几乎要把脖子打断。
cues.en: by a tremendous force nearly snapping off his neck.

cues.zh: 加一个中间帧，他的头像是被擀面杖或其他东西打了一下。
cues.en: With one in-between his head has been hit by a rolling pin or some other object.

cues.zh: 加两个中间帧，他像是肌肉抽搐了一下。
cues.en: With two in-betweens, he has a muscle twitch.

cues.zh: 加三个中间帧，他像是在躲开擀面杖或其他东西。
cues.en: With three in-betweens, he's dodging the rolling pin or the other object.

cues.zh: 再往前，他像是在说“走开，别在这儿”。
cues.en: Before he's saying moving get out of here.

cues.zh: 加五个中间帧，他更友好地说“过来这边。来吧。快点。”
cues.en: With five, he's more friendly saying over here. Come on. Hurry.

cues.zh: 加六个中间帧，他看到了一个漂亮姑娘，或者他一直想要的那辆跑车。
cues.en: With six, he sees a good-looking girl, or the sports car he always wanted.

cues.zh: 画到七张时，他想更仔细地看看某个东西。
cues.en: With seven, he's trying to get a better look at something.

cues.zh: 画到八张时，他在厨房架子上找花生酱。
cues.en: With eight, he's searching for the peanut butter on the kitchen shelf.

cues.zh: 画到九张时，他若有所思地打量着什么东西。
cues.en: With nine, he is appraising something very thoughtfully.

cues.zh: 画到十张中间帧时，他在伸展一块酸痛的肌肉。
cues.en: And with ten in-betweens, he is stretching a sore muscle.

cues.zh: 电影的标准帧率是每秒24帧。
cues.en: The standard frame rate for movies is 24 frames per second.

cues.zh: 如果每一帧都画一张，就是每秒24张，
cues.en: If one drawing is made for each frame 24 drawings per second,

cues.zh: 这叫一拍一。
cues.en: that is called drawing on once.

cues.zh: 如果每两帧画一张，
cues.en: If one drawing is made for every two frames,

cues.zh: 这叫一拍二。
cues.en: that's called drawing on twos.

cues.zh: 每三帧画一张就是三拍，以此类推。
cues.en: And every three drawings is threes and so on.

cues.zh: 其实一拍二比一拍一常见得多，原因有几个。
cues.en: It's actually very common to draw on twos than once for a few reasons.

cues.zh: 第一，它把工作量减半。
cues.en: First it cuts the amount of work in half.

cues.zh: 第二，它实际上让缓慢的动作比逐帧画看起来更流畅。
cues.en: Second it actually makes slow actions look smoother than if you were to draw every frame.

cues.zh: 因为在两个非常接近的图之间绘制所需的精度
cues.en: Because the precision needed to draw in between two very close drawings

cues.zh: 会导致动画看起来抖动。
cues.en: can lead to the animation looking jittery.

cues.zh: 也有人认为一拍二更适合快速动作。
cues.en: Some would also say that drawing on twos is better for fast actions as well.

cues.zh: 因为它能给动画带来闪光和灵气
cues.en: Because it gives a sparkle and spirit to the animation

cues.zh: 如果一拍一的话，时间分配会过于均匀，显得不够生动。
cues.en: that would otherwise be too evenly timed and less lively if it were drawn on once.

cues.zh: 但当有需要被看清的非常快速的动作时，一拍一是必要的
cues.en: But drawing on ones is necessary when there's a very fast action that needs to be read

cues.zh: 通常是混乱或一连串密集的动作。
cues.en: often to scramble or a flurry of activity.

cues.zh: 而且每个姿势之间插入多少张图是每个人的选择。
cues.en: And it's also everyone's choice how many drawings to put in between poses.

cues.zh: 有些人会根据动作幅度大小来画更多或更少的中间帧。
cues.en: Some people draw more or less streams depending on how much movement there is.

cues.zh: 这能给动画带来非常动态的效果。
cues.en: This can give a very dynamic effect to the animation.

cues.zh: 所以下一个原理叫做夸张。
cues.en: So the next principle is called exaggeration.

cues.zh: 基本上每个动作、姿态和表情都可以提升一个层次
cues.en: Basically every action, pose and expression can be taken to the next level

cues.zh: 来增强对观众的冲击力。
cues.en: to increase the amount of impact on the viewer.

cues.zh: 所以早期迪士尼的动画师们会感到困惑
cues.en: So the early animators that Disney would get confused

cues.zh: 因为 Walt 让他们增加更多真实感，
cues.en: because Walt would tell them to add more realism,

cues.zh: 但改完之后他又会批评结果
cues.en: but then when they changed it he would criticize the result

cues.zh: 因为夸张得还不够。
cues.en: because it wasn't exaggerated enough.

cues.zh: 在 Walt 看来，这两者大概没什么区别
cues.en: In walt's mind, there was probably no difference

cues.zh: 让画面更真实，并不意味着让物理规律和比例更贴近现实。
cues.en: making it more realistic didn't mean make the physics and proportions more consistent with reality.

cues.zh: 而是让动作的理念或本质更明显、更真实。
cues.en: But rather make the idea or essence of the action more apparent and real.

cues.zh: 所以如果角色悲伤，就让他更悲伤。
cues.en: So if a character was sad, make him sadder.

cues.zh: 明亮，就让它更明亮。
cues.en: Bright, make him brighter.

cues.zh: 担忧，就让他更担忧。
cues.en: Worried, make him more worried.

cues.zh: 狂野，就让它更狂野。
cues.en: Wild, make him wilder.

cues.zh: 夸张不是更扭曲，而是更有说服力。
cues.en: Exaggeration doesn't mean more distorted, but more convincing.

cues.zh: 你总能加上夸张效果，这很厉害。
cues.en: It's amazing how you can always add exaggeration.

cues.zh: 这个动画看起来完成了，对吧？
cues.en: This animation looks finished, right?

cues.zh: 但我们来加点夸张效果。
cues.en: But let's give it some exaggeration.

cues.zh: 现在对比这两个，
cues.en: Now when we compare the two,

cues.zh: 第一个明显看起来没那么有力量，
cues.en: the first one definitely looks less powerful

cues.zh: 尽管之前我们觉得它已经完成了。
cues.en: even though earlier we thought it was finished.

cues.zh: 动作快的时候，夸张幅度要更大才能被注意到。
cues.en: When motions are quick, the exaggeration needs to be bigger in order to be noticed.

cues.zh: 这个定格画面看起来太夸张了，不真实。
cues.en: This still frame looks way too extreme to be realistic.

cues.zh: 但播放起来看就没那么夸张了。
cues.en: But when you play it in motion it looks less extreme.

cues.zh: 这是因为短时间内眼睛感知到的很多帧
cues.en: That's because a lot of the frames that your eye perceives in a short time

cues.zh: 都是不太夸张的帧，只有一帧非常夸张。
cues.en: are less extreme frames and only one of them is very extreme.

cues.zh: 所以为了增强它的存在感，你可以让它停留更久，
cues.en: So in order to boost its presence you can either make it stay on the screen longer

cues.zh: 或者让它更夸张。
cues.en: or make it more extreme.

cues.zh: 因为很难判断还有多少夸张空间，
cues.en: Since it's hard to tell how much room you have for exaggeration,

cues.zh: 一个好法则是把夸张推到真的过头为止。
cues.en: a good rule to follow is to push the exaggeration level until it actually becomes too much.

cues.zh: 然后倒回去，直到你满意为止。
cues.en: Then wind it back until you're satisfied with it.

cues.zh: 这样你就能事先看到整个范围，而不是盲目尝试。
cues.en: This way you see the whole range beforehand instead of shooting in the dark.

cues.zh: 所以下一个原则叫做扎实的绘画。
cues.en: So the next principle is called solid drawing.

cues.zh: 这个原则是关于确保形体感觉像是处在三维空间中
cues.en: This principle is about making sure that forms feel like they are in three-dimensional space

cues.zh: 具有体积、重量和平衡感。
cues.en: with volume weight and balance.

cues.zh: 让动画制作轻松很多的一件事，是能够从各个角度绘制人物。
cues.en: One thing that makes animating a lot easier is being able to draw a figure from all angles.

cues.zh: 这需要三维绘画的知识。
cues.en: This requires knowledge of three-dimensional drawing.

cues.zh: 例如，在球体上画一条线时
cues.en: For example when drawing a line on a sphere

cues.zh: 它必须沿着球体表面的轮廓走。
cues.en: it must follow the contour of the spheres surface.

cues.zh: 一条直线会立刻让圆形看起来扁平。
cues.en: A straight line instantly makes the circle look flat.

cues.zh: 画立方体时，避免画平行线。
cues.en: When drawing cubes, avoid making parallel lines.

cues.zh: 线条应该向消失点弯曲。
cues.en: Lines should be bent towards the vanishing point.

cues.zh: 否则，它看起来会像一个扁平的符号或标志。
cues.en: Otherwise, it will look like a flat symbol or a logo.

cues.zh: 画角色草图时
cues.en: When doing a rough pass of the character

cues.zh: 用球体、立方体和圆柱体等基本立体形状
cues.en: use basic solid shapes like spheres, cubes and cylinders

cues.zh: 来构建角色，而不是用圆形、正方形和矩形。
cues.en: to construct the character instead of circles squares and rectangles.

cues.zh: 这有助于你留意其中的空间感。
cues.en: This will help you be mindful of the space therein.

cues.zh: 另一件事是，你可以在地面上画透视线
cues.en: Another thing you can do is draw perspective lines on the ground

cues.zh: 来追踪它们与相机的距离
cues.en: to keep track of their distance from the camera

cues.zh: 这样你就能知道何时该画大或画小。
cues.en: so that you can know when to draw them bigger or smaller.

cues.zh: 进入角色的清线版本时
cues.en: When moving on to the clean line version of your character

cues.zh: 要非常注意遮挡关系，尽可能把它加进去。
cues.en: be very mindful of overlap and try to include it whenever possible.

cues.zh: 没有遮挡，一切看起来都在同一平面上。
cues.en: Without overlap everything appears to be on the same plane.

cues.zh: 但只要这里那里加一条线
cues.en: But just adding a single line here and there

cues.zh: 就能界定哪些表面凸出、哪些后退。
cues.en: can define where surfaces come out and where they recede.

cues.zh: 画线时还要注意的一点是避免对称。
cues.en: Another thing to note when doing lines is to avoid symmetry.

cues.zh: 对称的线条看起来平淡。
cues.en: Symmetrical lines look flat.

cues.zh: 试着把直线和曲线搭配起来
cues.en: Try to pair a straight line with a curved line

cues.zh: 或者让两条曲线错开。
cues.en: or offset two curved lines.

cues.zh: 这样看起来更自然、更有动感。
cues.en: So it looks more natural and dynamic.

cues.zh: 扎实绘画的原则同样适用于3D动画。
cues.en: The principle of solid drawing applies to 3D animation as well.

cues.zh: 在表现角色的姿态时，要体现重量感和平衡感。
cues.en: In regards to portraying weight and balance in the pose of a character.

cues.zh: 比如避免所谓的“对称重复”
cues.en: For example avoid what's called twinning

cues.zh: 也就是手臂、腿和其他成对部位做完全相同的动作。
cues.en: which happens when the arms and legs and other paired features are doing the exact same thing.

cues.zh: 这是动画师们都知道的通病，必须刻意去避免
cues.en: This is a known affliction that animators have to make a conscious effort to avoid

cues.zh: 可以往一侧倾斜，或者把一只手放在胯上
cues.en: instead lean it over to one side or put one hand on the hips

cues.zh: 或者让它驼着背，做点什么来体现它有重量
cues.en: or give it a slouch or do something to show that it has weight

cues.zh: 并且在3D环境中必须保持平衡。
cues.en: and has to keep its balance in a 3D environment.

cues.zh: 好了。动画的最后一条原则叫吸引力。
cues.en: Alright. The last principle of animation is called appeal.

cues.zh: 你制作动画的角色，基本上应该看着让人舒服。
cues.en: Basically characters that you animate should be somewhat pleasing to look at.

cues.zh: 他们得有某种讨人喜欢的魅力特质。
cues.en: They should have some kind of charismatic aspect to like about them.

cues.zh: 这不仅适用于故事的主角，
cues.en: This doesn't only apply to the hero of the story,

cues.zh: 也适用于反派和其他所有角色
cues.en: but also the villain and every other character

cues.zh: 吸引力并不总是指好看。
cues.en: Appeal doesn't always mean good-looking.

cues.zh: 也可以指有趣。
cues.en: It can also mean interesting.

cues.zh: 所以反派也应该讨人喜欢，意思是他们看起来有意思。
cues.en: So the villain should be likable in the sense that they are interesting to look at.

cues.zh: 麻烦的是，每个人对吸引力的标准都不一样。
cues.en: The tricky thing about this is that everyone has a different standard for what is appealing.

cues.zh: 不过，只要给角色设计出有动态感的外形，就能大大提升吸引力。
cues.en: However, just giving your character a dynamic design can greatly boost its appeal.

cues.zh: 做到这点有三步。
cues.en: Here are three steps to doing that.

cues.zh: 第一，使用多种形状
cues.en: First, use a variety of shapes

cues.zh: 而不是每个角色都用同一种形状。
cues.en: instead of using the same shape for every character.

cues.zh: 多尝试不同的形状
cues.en: Try out different shapes

cues.zh: 因为角色能有的奇葩造型是没有极限的。
cues.en: because there's no limit to the spectrum of crazy configurations that characters can have.

cues.zh: 每个好角色设计都始于清晰的形状。
cues.en: Every good character design starts with a clear shape.

cues.zh: 第二，玩转比例。
cues.en: Second, play with proportions.

cues.zh: 漫画家常常放大我们觉得有趣的部分
cues.en: Cartoonists often magnify the things we find interesting

cues.zh: 缩小我们可能觉得丑陋或无聊的部分。
cues.en: and shrink the things we might find ugly or boring.

cues.zh: 比如他们可能放大头部和眼睛
cues.en: For example they might enlarge the head and eyes

cues.zh: 缩小身体，把手画得更大。
cues.en: shrink the body and make the hands larger.

cues.zh: 找到定义角色性格的那个特征
cues.en: Finding the aspect of a character that defines his or her personality

cues.zh: 把它放大，往往能创造出更吸引人的设计。
cues.en: and blowing it up can often create a more appealing design.

cues.zh: 第三，保持简洁。
cues.en: Third, keep it simple.

cues.zh: 信息太多会让角色过于复杂
cues.en: Too much information can over complicate the character

cues.zh: 也会让动画制作更难、更受限。
cues.en: and also make it harder and more restraining to animate.

cues.zh: 这就是插画绘制和动画绘制的区别
cues.en: This is a difference between drawing for illustration and drawing for animation

cues.zh: 做动画角色时，你必须取舍保留哪些细节。
cues.en: with animated characters you have to pick and choose what details to keep.

cues.zh: 因为那些细节你要画上几百遍。
cues.en: Because you're going to be drawing those details hundreds of times.

cues.zh: 那我们来给几个角色做一下吸引力改造。
cues.en: So let's give some characters an appeal makeover.

cues.zh: 这个国王外形很普通，没什么个性。
cues.en: This king has a generic shape and not much personality.

cues.zh: 我们把它做得更像一颗蛋。
cues.en: Let's make it more like an egg.

cues.zh: 现在它的吸引力来自看起来骄傲、强大又娇小。
cues.en: Now his appeal comes from looking proud, powerful and petite.

cues.zh: 这个机器人雇佣兵细节太多，看不出任何个性。
cues.en: This robot mercenary has too many details to see any personality.

cues.zh: 我们挑几个细节并加以强调。
cues.en: Let's pick a few details and emphasize them.

cues.zh: 去掉其余的，再改变他的外形。
cues.en: Remove the rest and change his shape.

cues.zh: 现在他身上有一种神秘的吸引力。
cues.en: Now he has a mysterious appeal to him.

cues.zh: 这个渔夫看起来挺普通的。
cues.en: This fisherman looks pretty average.

cues.zh: 我们调整他的比例，强调他瘦长的身形。
cues.en: Let's adjust his proportions to emphasize his lankiness.

cues.zh: 并让这成为他的吸引力所在。
cues.en: and make that his point of appeal.

cues.zh: 这就是我关于吸引力的全部内容，也带我们来到了这个12部分系列的结尾。
cues.en: So that's all I've got for appeal and that brings us to the end of our 12 part series.

cues.zh: 感谢你的观看。
cues.en: So I thank you for watching it.

cues.zh: 我做得很开心，而且我也确实学到了很多关于动画的知识。
cues.en: I had a lot of fun making it and I actually learned a lot about animation, too.

cues.zh: 我确实打算继续做这些视频
cues.en: I do plan to continue making these videos

cues.zh: 接下来我会讲走路和跑步循环。
cues.en: and next I will be covering walk and run cycles.

cues.zh: 感谢观看，我们下个视频见
cues.en: So thanks for watching and I'll see you in the next video
